fichas.title: Open Fireplaces
fichas.summary: Open fireplaces must be structurally stable and made from noncombustible materials, such as fireclay, suitable bricks or blocks, fireproof concrete, or grey cast iron; smoke hoods may be steel, brass, or copper sheet. Each fireplace requires its own appropriately sized chimney. The fireplace and chimney should be adjacent, and the flue pipe connects to the chimney at the stated angle. Adequate air supply is required, and combustible components and objects must be kept clear of the combustion chamber. The page illustrates fireplace layouts, construction and floor protection, and provides a dimension table for fireplace types.

dimensions.label: Minimum room floor area
dimensions.context: Open fireplaces must not be installed in rooms with less than this floor area.

dimensions.label: Effective chimney height
dimensions.context: At least; measured from the smoke flue connection to the chimney top.
dimensions.ocr_raw:
CHIMNEYS AND VENTILATION SHAFTS
Open Fireplaces

Open fireplaces must be structurally stable and made of noncombustible building materials. They can be built of fireclay
blocks or slabs, bricks or blocks suitable for chimney construction,
fireproof concrete or grey cast iron. Smoke hoods can be made of
steel, brass or copper sheet.
